title: Program Manager II, New Product Introduction, Google Data Center
description:
### **Minimum qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
* 2 years of experience in program or project management.
* Experience in supply chain management and New Product Introduction (NPI).
* Experience in hardware manufacturing.

  

### **Preferred qualifications:**

* 2 years of experience managing cross-functional or cross-team projects.
* Expertise with a multi-level bill of materials structuring and tracking, combined with supply-demand planning and project budget reconciliation.
* Proven track record executing strategic inventory risk buys, buffer stock strategies, and component second-sourcing to de-risk ramp timelines.
* Strong investigative mindset with the ability to pivot seamlessly between granular data analysis and executive-level strategic communication.

**About the job**
-----------------

A problem isn’t truly solved until it’s solved for all. That’s why Googlers build products that help create opportunities for everyone, whether down the street or across the globe. As a Program Manager at Google, you’ll lead complex, multi-disciplinary projects from start to finish — working with stakeholders to plan requirements, manage project schedules, identify risks, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. Your projects will often span offices, time zones, and hemispheres. It's your job to coordinate the players and keep them up to date on progress and deadlines.

Google is looking for a dynamic professional to lead all aspects of supply chain readiness in New Product Introduction (NPI) products for our global data centers.

As a Supply Chain Program Manager, you work with cross-functional teams starting with product inception to volume ramp to bring innovative products into global data centers efficiently and dynamically. description:

Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.
